bug_semantics: A crafted NFS server can place an attacker-controlled 32-bit ZDR string length in an RPC reply. libnfs_zdr_string reads that uint32_t length and, through 6.0.2, relies on an overflow-prone bounds expression instead of first proving that the length fits in the receive buffer. In the original implementation, adding uint32_t size to signed int pos converts the addition to unsigned arithmetic and can wrap; in 6.0.2, the explicit (int)size conversion can turn a value above INT_MAX negative so the check passes. Later indexing, allocation, termination, and opaque-copy logic can consequently operate beyond the received buffer. The fix rejects size values larger than zdrs->size before the cast/addition.
flaw_origin: Commit 763cd6e3e2bbb6906186e7ed6a86660276b596b7 introduced libnfs's built-in ZDR implementation and first created libnfs_zdr_string in lib/libnfs-zdr.c. Its new lines 226-243 decoded an untrusted uint32_t size, checked only zdrs->pos + size > zdrs->size, then allocated size + 1, wrote the terminator, and copied size bytes. include/libnfs-zdr.h lines 70-74 defined buffer size and position as int, making the mixed signed/unsigned bound overflow-prone. The direct parent has no lib/libnfs-zdr.c at all, so this is the smallest repository commit that first wrote the vulnerable mechanism rather than a later move or refactor.
ai_marker: absent — the raw BIC commit object records author Ronnie Sahlberg <ronniesahlberg@gmail.com> and committer Ronnie Sahlberg <ronniesahlberg@gmail.com>; its message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or other AI trailer, and neither identity is a bot
evidence: Advisory evidence: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-379r-2p3h-m47v and https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-53689 both identify CVE-2026-53689 in libnfs through 6.0.2, the missing string-size validation in libnfs_zdr_string, crafted-NFS-server reachability, and upstream fix 55c18ea33a83d667f79f0ef209c96895795c729f. First-party upstream BIC URL: https://github.com/sahlberg/libnfs/commit/763cd6e3e2bbb6906186e7ed6a86660276b596b7; git log -L and git log -S across the full clone trace the first function addition to that commit, where lib/libnfs-zdr.c:218-247 contains the new function and lines 226-243 contain the flawed decode/bounds/allocation/copy sequence; include/libnfs-zdr.h:70-74 confirms int size and int pos. Raw git show identifies its sole direct parent as 061d3f1f99e354af36e8ac259a98f863975e51f5. Direct-parent verification with git cat-file -e 061d3f1f99e354af36e8ac259a98f863975e51f5:lib/libnfs-zdr.c fails because the path does not exist, proving the vulnerable lines absent. First-party upstream fix URL: https://github.com/sahlberg/libnfs/commit/55c18ea33a83d667f79f0ef209c96895795c729f; it is a one-parent direct source fix whose parent f0b109df8fd865a2f8d39e78310fd875e15f3ac1 still has only the vulnerable check at lib/libnfs-zdr.c:322, while the fix adds if (size > zdrs->size) return FALSE at lines 321-324 of the fix diff before the overflow-prone expression. Version evidence: git tag --contains 763cd6e3e2bbb6906186e7ed6a86660276b596b7 starts with libnfs-1.5.0 and includes libnfs-6.0.2; libnfs-1.5.0:lib/libnfs-zdr.c:232-256 contains the flawed implementation, and libnfs-6.0.2:lib/libnfs-zdr.c:297-324 contains the vulnerable pre-fix form. git tag --contains 55c18ea33a83d667f79f0ef209c96895795c729f returns libnfs-7.0.0 and libnfs-7.0.1 only; libnfs-7.0.0:lib/libnfs-zdr.c:338-345 contains the new size check, establishing 6.0.2 as the last vulnerable upstream tag and 7.0.0 as the first fixed upstream tag. The BIC raw commit object contains no AI marker.
reasoning: The audit began from the advisory's named function and direct fix. The fix parent demonstrates the vulnerable lifecycle endpoint: an untrusted wire uint32_t reaches a signed/cast overflow-prone bounds expression without an independent size sanity check, and 55c18ea33a83d667f79f0ef209c96895795c729f closes that exact gap before any cast, addition, index, allocation, or copy. Line history then follows the flawed mechanism backward past later edits to 763cd6e3e2bbb6906186e7ed6a86660276b596b7, which created the function with the same missing validation and mixed signed/unsigned overflowing sum. Because the function's entire source file is absent from its immediate parent, the parent-tree test proves introduction rather than merely blame continuity. The commit has one parent and no evidence of a squash to decompose, so no member SHA supplants it. Tag membership places the BIC in releases beginning with 1.5.0 and through advisory-affected 6.0.2, while the direct fix first appears in 7.0.0. Finally, AI attribution is restricted to the BIC commit object: its human author and committer and trailer-free message provide no AI signal. The causally proven closed verdict is therefore NOT_AI.
